name: Pure Procrastination Scale
construct: Core procrastination as irrational delay, drawn from the strongest items of the General Procrastination Scale, the Adult Inventory of Procrastination and the Decisional Procrastination Questionnaire.
licence: Items reproduced in full in Svartdal et al. (2016, 2017), Frontiers in Psychology: "This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)." No separate author licence statement for the PPS was located.

responseOptions.label: Very seldom or not true of me
Very often true, or true with me

items.text: I delay making decision until it's too late.
items.note: Svartdal et al. (2016) quote this item as 'I delay making decisions until it's too late'; the 2017 Table 1 wording is retained here.

items.text: Even after I make a decision I delay acting upon it.
I waste a lot of time on trivial matters before getting to the final decisions.
In preparation for some deadlines, I often waste time by doing other things.
Even jobs that require little else except sitting down and doing them. I find that they seldom get done for days.
items.note: Table 1 splits this item across two rows; the full stop after 'them' is as printed and is probably a comma in the original.

items.text: I often find myself performing tasks that I had intended to do days before
I am continually saying “I’ll do it tomorrow.”
I generally delay before starting on work I have to do.
I find myself running out of time.
items.note: Svartdal et al. (2017) recommend deleting this item because it may index busyness rather than procrastination.

items.text: I don't get things done on time.
I am not very good at meeting deadlines.
Putting things off till the last minute has cost me money in the past.

subscales.name: Decisional delay
subscales.description: Items drawn from the Decisional Procrastination Questionnaire.

subscales.name: Implemental delay
subscales.description: Irrational delay in starting or carrying out tasks; items drawn from the General Procrastination Scale. Recommended as a 5 item short form.

subscales.name: Timeliness or lateness
subscales.description: Delay in meeting deadlines; items drawn from the Adult Inventory of Procrastination.

scoring: No reverse scored items. Sum or average the items for the total and for each of the 3 factors; higher scores indicate more procrastination. No published cut offs. Svartdal et al. (2016) report European sample item means of about 2.3 to 2.8 and recommend the 5 item implemental delay form (items 4 to 8) as the purest measure.
citation: Steel, P. (2010). Arousal, avoidant and decisional procrastinators: Do they exist? Personality and Individual Differences, 48(8), 926–934. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.paid.2010.02.025
transcriptionNote: Items transcribed from Table 1 of Svartdal et al. (2017), Frontiers in Psychology 8:1927 (CC BY). Neither Frontiers article reproduces respondent instructions or labels for scale points 2 to 4; only the endpoints are quoted (1 'Very seldom or not true of me', 5 'Very often true, or true with me'), so points 2 to 4 are left unlabelled. Steel (2010) itself was not consulted. Minor wording differences between the 2016 and 2017 articles are noted on items 1 and 5.
